stem: The modern periodic table consists of ______ periods.
solution: The modern periodic table consists of \(7\) periods.

stem: The formula of the chloride of metal M is \(\mathrm{MCl_2}\). The metal M belongs to ______ group.
solution: The metal M belongs to the \(2^{\mathrm{nd}}\) group. Since the valency of M is 2 (it combines with two chlorine atoms), it belongs to group 2.

stem: Corrosion can be prevented by using ______ solution.
solution: Corrosion can be prevented by using anti-rust solution.

stem: Voltmeter, ammeter, galvanometer, thermometer.
solution: Odd one out: thermometer. A thermometer is a device used for measuring temperature. The other devices are used to measure current and potential difference in a circuit.

stem: Loudspeaker, bar magnet, electric motor, microphone.
solution: Odd one out: bar magnet. In the other devices, one form of energy is converted to another form of energy.

stem: Reaction of iron nails with copper sulphate solution is an example of
solution: Displacement reaction. When a more reactive element removes another element having less reactivity from its compound, the reaction is termed a displacement reaction. In the reaction of iron nails with copper sulphate solution, iron displaces copper from the copper sulphate solution: \(\mathrm{CuSO_4(aq) + Fe(s) \rightarrow FeSO_4(aq) + Cu(s)}\).

stem: Dilute NaOH can be tested with
solution: Red litmus paper. Sodium hydroxide when dissolved in water dissociates: \(\mathrm{NaOH(s) \rightarrow Na^{+}_{(aq)} + OH^{-}_{(aq)}}\). The dissociated \(\mathrm{OH^{-}}\) ions turn moist red litmus paper blue.

subtopic: Series and Parallel Combination of Resistors
stem: In series combination which remains constant?
solution: Current. When a potential difference is applied across a combination of resistors in series, the same current flows through each resistor.

stem: An object of 10 cm is placed in front of a plane mirror. The height of image will be ______.
solution: 10 cm. The image formed by a plane mirror is always of the same size as that of the object.

stem: When a ray of light travels from air to glass slab and strikes the surface of separation at \(90^\circ\), then it ______.
solution: Passes unbent. When the ray strikes the surface of separation at \(90^\circ\) (i.e. along the normal), the angle of incidence \(i\) is zero and so also the angle of refraction. Hence the ray passes undeviated.

stem: Define: 1 volt PD (potential difference).
solution: The potential difference between two points is said to be 1 volt if 1 joule of work is done in moving 1 coulomb of electric charge from one point to another. \(1\ \mathrm{volt\ (V)} = \dfrac{1\ \mathrm{joule\ (J)}}{1\ \mathrm{coulomb\ (C)}}\).

stem: Define: Electric power.
solution: Electric power is the electric work done per unit time. Its SI unit is watt (W). \(\mathrm{Electric\ power}\ (P) = \dfrac{\mathrm{Electric\ work}\ (W)}{\mathrm{Time}\ (t)}\).

stem: What major harm is done to the human beings by air pollution?
solution:
Air pollution has major effects on human health. They can be short-term effects or long-term effects.

Short-term effects:
- Irritation of eyes, nose, mouth and throat
- Infections of the respiratory tract such as bronchitis and pneumonia
- Headache, nausea and allergy
- Asthmatic attacks
- Reduced lung functioning

Long-term effects:
- Chronic pulmonary disease
- Cardiovascular disease
- Lung cancer
- Premature death

stem: Calculate the focal length of a corrective lens having power \(+2\,\mathrm{D}\).
solution:
Given: Power \(P = +2\,\mathrm{D}\).
\(P = \dfrac{1}{f}\)
\(\therefore f = \dfrac{1}{P} = \dfrac{1}{2} = 0.5\ \mathrm{m}\).
The focal length of the corrective lens is \(0.5\ \mathrm{m}\).

stem: Write two applications of sodium bicarbonate (baking soda).
solution:
Applications of sodium bicarbonate (any two):
- It is used to prepare light and spongy bread, cakes and dhoklas.
- Being alkaline, it helps reduce acidity in the stomach.
- It is very useful in preparing \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) gas, and it is one of the contents of fire extinguishers.

stem: A simple microscope is used by watch repairers. Give reason.
solution: When an object is placed within the focal length of a simple microscope, its magnified and erect image is obtained on the same side of the lens as that of the object. So, a watch repairer sees the minute parts of a watch very clearly with a simple microscope by adjusting the distance between the object and the lens. This helps in repairing the watch. Hence, a simple microscope is used by watch repairers.

stem: Draw a neat and labelled diagram of the pH scale.
solution: The pH scale (range of pH values) runs from 0 to 14. pH 0 to less than 7 is acidic, pH 7 is neutral, and pH greater than 7 to 14 is alkaline (basic). Around pH 0-1 is strongly acidic, near pH 6 is weakly acidic, near pH 8 is weakly alkaline, and around pH 13-14 is strongly alkaline. A colour band is shown along the scale (Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo, Violet). Label the acidic region (0 to 7), the neutral point (7), and the alkaline region (7 to 14).

subtopic: Early Attempts and Mendeleev's Periodic Table
stem: What are the main features of Mendeleev's periodic table?
solution:
Main features of Mendeleev's periodic table:
- The horizontal rows in the periodic table are called periods. There are seven periods. These are numbered from 1 to 7.
- Properties of elements in a particular period show regular gradation from left to right.
- Vertical columns in the periodic table are called groups. There are eight groups numbered from I to VIII. Groups I to VII are further divided into A and B subgroups.

stem: Define 'redox reaction'. Give one example.
solution:
When oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously in a given chemical reaction, it is known as a redox reaction.

Example: \(\mathrm{BaSO_4 + 4C \rightarrow BaS + 4CO}\). Here \(\mathrm{BaSO_4}\) is reduced to \(\mathrm{BaS}\) (reduction) while carbon is oxidised to \(\mathrm{CO}\) (oxidation), so both occur simultaneously.

solution:
Two possible reasons are:

b) Because of shortening of the eye ball or flattening of the eye lens.

stem: What is refraction of light? How is it related to refractive index?
solution:
The phenomenon of a change in the direction of the propagation of light when it passes obliquely from one transparent medium to another is called refraction of light.

For a given angle of incidence, the extent of refraction of light is different in different media (this depends on the refractive index):
- When the refractive index of the second medium is greater than the refractive index of the first medium, the refracted ray bends more towards the normal.
- When the refractive index of the first medium is greater than the refractive index of the second medium, the refracted ray bends away from the normal.

stem: Explain how spectrum is formed.
solution:
When white light passes through a glass prism, it spreads out into a band of different colours called the spectrum of light.
- When white light is dispersed into seven colours by a glass prism, different colours bend through different angles with respect to the incident ray.
- The sequence of colours given by the prism is Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange and Red.
- Of the seven colours, red light bends the least, while violet light bends the most. So, the rays of each colour emerge along different paths and appear distinct. Hence, we get a spectrum of seven different colours.

context: Suggest measures in the following situations:
stem: To avoid noise pollution in the classroom.
solution:
Measures to avoid noise pollution in the classroom:
- When the teacher is not present in the classroom, all students should observe silence and not shout loudly.
- Activities such as book reading, solo singing or storytelling should be carried out so that the other students can maintain silence.
- The monitors in the class who control the classroom should ask the teacher to punish the students who make a lot of noise.
- Add curtains to the classroom.
- Use cork bulletin boards for the walls.
- Place sound-absorbent panels on the upper walls of the classroom.

context: Suggest measures in the following situations:
stem: To minimize electricity consumption at home.
solution:
The following practices should be adopted to minimise electricity consumption at home:
- Switch off the fans, lights and bulbs when not in use.
- Use of CFL should be encouraged.
- Avoid using air conditioners whenever possible.
- Allow sunlight and fresh air to enter the house to reduce the use of electricity during the day time.
- Use solar water heaters instead of electrical heaters.

context: Suggest measures in the following situations:
stem: Bursting fire crackers in festivals and processions.
solution:
The following steps should be adopted to minimise the bursting of fire crackers in festivals and processions:
- Bursting fire crackers should be strictly avoided because they cause noise and air pollution.
- If necessary, noiseless crackers or eco-friendly variety of crackers can be used.
- Fire crackers should not be burst near hospitals and other silence zones.
- Bursting of fire crackers should be banned after 10 p.m.

subtopic: Series and Parallel Combination of Resistors
stem: Find the expression for the resistors connected in series and write the two characteristics of it. (Draw figure.)
solution:
Expression for resistors in series: \(R_1\), \(R_2\) and \(R_3\) are three resistors connected in series between points C and D. \(I\) is the current and \(V\) is the PD across points C and D. \(R_s\) is the effective resistance and \(V_1\), \(V_2\), \(V_3\) are the potentials across the three resistors, such that
\(V = V_1 + V_2 + V_3\) ... (1)
Using Ohm's law, \(V = I R_s\), and \(V_1 = I R_1\), \(V_2 = I R_2\), \(V_3 = I R_3\).
Substituting in Equation (1): \(I R_s = I R_1 + I R_2 + I R_3\)
\(\therefore R_s = R_1 + R_2 + R_3\).
For n resistors in series: \(R_s = R_1 + R_2 + R_3 + R_4 + \cdots + R_n\).

Characteristics of a series combination of resistors (any two):
a) The same current flows through each resistor.
b) The effective resistance of the combination is greater than any of the resistances in the combination.
c) The effective resistance of the combination is equal to the sum of individual resistors.

stem: Explain 'Electric motor' with the help of the following points: (i) Draw figure (ii) Principle of Electric motor (iii) Name any four appliances where electric motor is used.
solution:
(i) Figure: A labelled diagram of an electric motor showing the armature coil ABCD wound on an iron core placed between the N and S poles of a magnet, the split ring commutator, the brushes B1 and B2, the axle, and the battery with a key.
(ii) Principle of Electric Motor: An electric motor works on the principle that a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field experiences a force.
(iii) Appliances (any four): Electric motors are used in domestic appliances such as a mixer, blender and washing machine. A DC motor is used in an electric fan, hair dryer, record player, tape recorder and blower.
